question: In 1887, the Royal Society, London gave the Davy Medal for the ‘discovery of the periodic law of chemical elements’ to _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**John Alexander Newland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1887, the Royal Society, London** gave the **Davy Medal **for the **‘discovery of the periodic law of chemical elements’ **to **John Alexander Newland**.
 
• British chemist, **John Alexander Reina Newlands** specialised in **elemental periodicity**.
 
• **John Newlands **was the first to create a **table of chemical elements grouped according to their respective atomic weight**.
 
• He made his idea of the **periodicity of the chemical elements**, which he had arranged in order of atomic weight, public in** 1864**.
 
• In order to make a **connection with musical octaves**, Newlands named this phenomenon,** The Law of Octaves** after noticing **commonalities between elements whose atomic weights varied by seven**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The first person to arrange chemical elements according to their atomic weights was** AEB de Chancourtois**, who also created an **early version of the periodic table known as the "telluric helix" because tellurium was in the centre**.
 
• Russian chemist and inventor **Dmitri Ivanovich Mendeleev** is best known for conceiving th**e Periodic Law and developing a preliminary version of the periodic table of elements**.
 
• A pioneer in creating the** first iterations of the periodic table of chemical elements** was the German chemist **Julius Lothar Meyer**.
